text.p: Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd (SHC) chairman Dick Warburton said on Monday he welcomed the planned agreement which will see Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) take control of the Sydney casino's management contract.
PBL said it would buy an 85 percent stake in the casino's management contract for A$240 million from Showboat Inc.
Warburton said PBL had indicated that Neil Gamble would remain chief executive officer of SHC.
"In other words, Mr Gamble will continue to be in charge of the day to day operations of casino which means there will be a smooth transition," Warburton said in a statement.
Gamble was appointed to his position in November.
Warburton said PBL would bring a range of benefits to Sydney Harbour Casino.
"As an Australian company they obviously have a range of government and business contacts which can only be of assistance to us," Warburton said.
"Kerry Packer, who is a director of the company (PBL) is extremely well known in the gaming industry around the world and this will also boost our profile enormously," he said.
Under the PBL-Showboat deal Packer's media group would buy a 10 percent stake in SHC for A$1.85 per share.
Warburton said Showboat would still be a major shareholder in Sydney Harbour Casino and would continue to provide valuable assistance to the company.
"The planned agreement between Showboat and PBL is subject to a series of approvals from the Casino Control Authority and other parties which are likely to take several months to obtain," he said.
"But if everything runs smoothly, PBL will be in a position to take up the management duties in the lead up to the opening of the permanent casino," he added.
